title: Mathematical model for non-monotone dose response to the PD-L1 blockade in vitro
task: Model non-monotonic dose-response curves for PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitors in T-cell co-culture
key_results: Estimated Cmax_resp (maximal safe concentration) and EC50 (potency) from luminescence trajectories; model explains non-monotonic response across full dose range by separating target-specific activation from concentration-dependent toxicity
comments: The approach elegantly addresses a common drug screening challenge, though validation against independent datasets and comparison to empirical fitting methods would strengthen claims of mechanistic superiority.

model_io.model: Ordinary differential equation system for T-cell reactivation kinetics
inputs: Co-culture experimental data (T-cells + target cells + PD-L1 blocking compound)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Non-monotonic dose response arises from competition between T-cell activation (low dose) and compound-induced toxicity (high dose)
hypotheses.result: Model successfully fits non-monotonic luminescence curves and distinguishes target-specific from non-specific effects

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mechanistic ODE model enables more reliable Cmax_resp and EC50 extraction than empirical curve-fitting alone
hypotheses.result: Model provides coherent parameter estimates across entire dose range, supporting rational optimization strategies

title: Meta-attention fusion and adaptive optimization for explainable diagnosis of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in blood smears
task: Automated diagnosis of acute lymphoblastic leukemia from blood smear images using vision transformer-CNN fusion
key_results: ConfuNetHMA achieves 100% classification accuracy on ALL dataset, 97.39% on C-NMC dataset, ROC-AUC 0.994 for ALL subtype differentiation; integrates meta-attention fusion, vision transformer, CNN, and meta-learning-inspired optimizer selection
comments: Perfect classification accuracy on one dataset is noteworthy but warrants skepticism given dataset size; explainability integration (Grad-CAM, LIME, SHAP, Integrated Gradients) is commendable for clinical adoption.

model_io.model: ConfuNetHMA: vision transformer + CNN with meta-attention fusion + meta-learning optimizer selection module
outputs: LIME, SHAP, Integrated Gradients feature importance

hypotheses.hypothesis: Meta-attention fusion of global (transformer) and local (CNN) features improves ALL diagnosis accuracy
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; model achieves near-perfect classification and high explainability agreement

title: KadakExpress — a tissue-specific gene expression atlas of the Indian black chicken breed
task: Tissue-specific gene expression atlas and transcriptomic database for Indian black chicken breed
key_results: KadakExpress database catalogs 39,679 genes, 383,176 gene-to-GO associations, 5,727 Reactome pathway annotations across 16 Kadaknath tissues; 302 unique genes in brain, 1,608 unique genes across all tissues; quality control performed via FastQC
comments: Comprehensive transcriptomic resource valuable for breed conservation and functional genomics; downstream functional validation and disease-resistance pathway characterization recommended.

model_io.model: RNA-seq transcriptomics pipeline: quality control (FastQC) → mapping → transcript quantification → tissue-specific expression classification → pathway annotation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multi-tissue transcriptomic profiling identifies tissue-enriched genes and pathways underlying Kadaknath breed traits (black meat pigmentation, disease resistance, adaptation)
hypotheses.result: Supported; database established with comprehensive annotations; specific pathway/trait associations to be explored via future mechanistic studies

title: Adaptive noise and attention mechanisms based light-weight U-net based architecture for robust medical image denoising of retinal fundus images
task: Medical image denoising of retinal fundus images using noise-aware residual U-Net
key_results: NAR-UNet achieves PSNR 37.99 dB (STARE, 5-fold CV), PSNR 40.46 dB (Messidor), SSIM 0.946–0.953, pixel accuracy 0.9963–0.9990; hybrid loss combines MSE, SSIM, and Sobel-based gradient loss
comments: Strong image-quality metrics; however, downstream impact on DR diagnosis/lesion detection not evaluated, limiting assessment of clinical utility.

model_io.model: NAR-UNet: light-weight U-Net with adaptive noise module and attention mechanisms; trained with hybrid loss (MSE + SSIM + Sobel gradient)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adaptive noise injection and attention-based U-Net architecture improve retinal image denoising
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; NAR-UNet outperforms state-of-the-art denoising methods on STARE and Messidor datasets

title: Dynamical analysis and neural network approximation of a fractional-order predator–prey model with disease transmission
task: Fractional-order eco-epidemiological modeling with neural network approximation
key_results: Caputo fractional-order S-I-P model with fear effects shows smoother, more stable dynamics than integer-order case; feedforward neural network trained via Levenberg-Marquardt achieves high accuracy in solution approximation
comments: Hybrid framework is technically sound but practical applicability to real biological systems requires parameter estimation and validation against empirical data.

model_io.model: Fractional-order S-I-P eco-epidemiological model (Caputo derivatives) + feedforward neural network (Levenberg-Marquardt training)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fractional-order formulation better captures memory-dependent biological interactions
hypotheses.result: Supported; fractional-order system exhibits smoother, more stable behavior than integer-order analog

title: PRSEPTransformer-EEG: source-space sLORETA and residual transformers for robust motor imagery and execution EEG decoding
task: Motor imagery and execution EEG decoding via source-space projection and transformer neural networks
key_results: PRSEPTransformer-EEG achieves 99.53% accuracy on BCI Competition IV 2a (Beta band), 98.29% on BCI2000 four-class imagery, exceeding prior reported results; source-space sLORETA projection combined with squeeze-excitation residual blocks and transformer encoder
comments: Strong empirical results across three datasets and electrode configurations; architectural advantage over prior work is clear, though computational cost and real-time feasibility on embedded BCI systems not reported.

model_io.model: PRSEPTransformer-EEG: preprocessing → sLORETA source localization → squeeze-excitation residual blocks + positional-encoding transformer encoder
inputs: scalp EEG signals (gel-based, water-based, dry electrodes)
outputs: motor intention classification (motor imagery or execution)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Source-space projection combined with temporal attention improves motor EEG decoding accuracy and generalization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; source-space model outperforms sensor-space on high-density recordings; sparse electrode configurations benefit from sensor-level features

title: Exploring the multifaceted therapeutic potential of linalool in triple negative breast cancer integrating in vitro, in silico, and network pharmacology approaches
task: Network pharmacology and in silico investigation of linalool therapeutic potential in triple-negative breast cancer
key_results: Linalool shows 30% TNBC cell viability inhibition at 100 µg/mL, DPPH IC₅₀ = 51.87 ± 0.56 µg/mL (antioxidant); 34 common linalool-TNBC targets identified via SuperPred/GeneCard; docking affinity: TOP2A −5.108 kcal/mol, COX-1 −5.345 kcal/mol, NRF2 −3.329 kcal/mol; molecular dynamics confirms conformational stability
comments: Integrated in vitro-in silico workflow is systematic; however, moderate in vitro cytotoxicity and predicted binding affinities suggest linalool is preliminary candidate requiring mechanistic and functional validation.

model_io.model: Network pharmacology (SuperPred, GeneCard) → compound-target-pathway network (Cytoscape) → molecular docking (GLIDE) → MD simulations

hypotheses.hypothesis: Linalool modulates TNBC-related molecular pathways through multi-target mechanism involving TOP2A, COX-1, NRF2
hypotheses.result: Partially supported; in silico evidence suggests pathway involvement, but in vitro cytotoxicity is modest and functional validation absent

title: An explainable multi-modal graph learning framework with attention-based GCN-GAT for EEG-based depression detection
task: Explainable multimodal EEG-based depression detection using graph neural networks
key_results: Hybrid GCN-GAT model achieves 94.8 ± 7.5% accuracy and MCC 0.907 ± 0.134 on multimodal EEG; integrated explainability shows high agreement between Integrated Gradients and GradientSHAP
comments: Rigorous leakage-controlled evaluation and heterogeneity auditing strengthen findings; substantial cohort and modality dependence limits generalizability claims.

model_io.model: Hybrid GCN-GAT framework with subject-level population graph
outputs: feature importance via Integrated Gradients, GradientSHAP, Permutation Feature Importance

hypotheses.hypothesis: Subject-level relational modeling with controlled multimodal contribution improves depression detection
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; integrated framework achieves high accuracy with explicit heterogeneity assessment

title: Beyond full fine-tuning: towards enhanced generalizability in downstream ECG foundation model adaptation
task: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategies for ECG foundation model generalization
key_results: Selective PEFT outperforms full fine-tuning on out-of-domain ECG data; optimal strategy depends on scenario-specific characteristics
comments: Addresses practical overfitting risk in foundation models with limited downstream data, though comparative gains appear modest on in-domain tasks.

model_io.model: Self-DANA ECG foundation model with selective PEFT strategies (partial fine-tuning, BitFit, LayerNorm tuning, linear probing)
outputs: generalization metrics on in-domain and out-of-domain data

hypotheses.hypothesis: Selective PEFT reduces overfitting compared to full fine-tuning
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; PEFT improves generalization especially on out-of-domain ECG data

title: A minimalist 1-lead ECG beat classification without handcrafted morphological feature extraction for inter-patient, edge-oriented diagnosis
task: Inter-patient ECG beat classification on raw 1-lead signal without handcrafted feature extraction
key_results: SVM classifier on 64 raw ECG samples + RR interval achieves 90.8% overall accuracy (inter-patient DS1/DS2 evaluation); normal beats F1 = 0.95, ventricular ectopic F1 = 0.73; model size 680 KB, inference latency 0.297 ms per beat on CPU
comments: Practical edge-device implementation with minimal preprocessing; supraventricular ectopic beat misclassification consistent with literature, but clinical utility for arrhythmia screening not quantified.

model_io.model: SVM (RBF kernel) trained on compressed raw ECG beats (64 samples) + strictly causal RR interval values
inputs: 1-lead ECG signal (MIT-BIH), R-peak detected beat segments
outputs: AAMI beat class (5 classes: N, S, V, F, Q)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Minimal raw ECG samples and beat-timing information suffice for inter-patient ventricular ectopic beat detection without handcrafted morphological features
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 90.8% inter-patient accuracy achieved with 64 samples/beat, demonstrating sufficiency of local R-peak vicinity and RR intervals

title: Integrative transcriptomics and systems genetics position AKAP4 as an evolutionarily constrained network hub gene in human sperm cryopreservation
task: Integrative systems genetics identification of cryopreservation-sensitive genes in human sperm
key_results: AKAP4 identified as central hub in short-term cryostress network; RT-qPCR confirms significant AKAP4 transcript reduction post-cryopreservation; network analysis reveals cryostress-responsive pathways in cytoskeletal organization, phosphorylation signaling, proteostasis, and DNA repair; AKAP4 shows purifying selection and mammalian conservation
comments: Well-integrated multi-omics approach (transcriptomics, network modeling, population genetics, structural annotation) identifies biologically plausible hub gene; functional validation of AKAP4 involvement in cryoinjury remains pending.

model_io.model: Transcriptomic analysis (GSE225320) → protein-protein interaction network → co-expression analysis → population genetics → comparative genomics
inputs: publicly available transcriptomic and proteomic datasets

hypotheses.hypothesis: AKAP4 is a network hub and cryopreservation-sensitive biomarker for sperm motility pathways
hypotheses.result: Supported; AKAP4 downregulated post-cryopreservation, functionally connected to flagellar architecture and cAMP/PKA signaling, evolutionarily conserved under purifying selection

title: A selectivity-aware machine-learning workflow for prioritizing CDK2-biased kinase inhibitor candidates
task: Machine learning workflow for prioritizing selective CDK2 kinase inhibitors
key_results: Extra Trees models trained on CDK1/2/4/6/7/9 bioactivity data (7,067 records, 4,879 unique compounds); CDK2 model MAE = 0.523, R² = 0.607; predicted CDK2 selectivity margin enriches CDK2-biased compounds with ROC-AUC 0.921 (retrospective), 0.888 ± 0.061 (scaffold held-out); MM-GBSA rescoring identifies one compound with convergent CDK2 preference
comments: Well-designed selectivity-aware pipeline combining machine learning, chemoinformatics, and molecular modeling; modest R² suggests predictions require downstream validation.

model_io.model: Extra Trees multi-target kinase activity prediction (RDKit descriptors + Morgan fingerprints) → selectivity margin calculation → scaffold-guided generation → docking (SP/XP) → MM-GBSA rescoring

hypotheses.hypothesis: Predicted selectivity margin better enriches CDK2-biased compounds than predicted potency alone
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; selectivity-aware workflow identifies CDK2-favored analogs with high retroactive and cross-validated enrichment

title: Iterative reconstruction algorithms for limited-angle tomography of thin slab objects: a performance review
task: Limited-angle tomographic reconstruction of thin-slab objects
key_results: Iterative algorithms (SIRT, CGLS, ASD-POCS, ML-EM) improve contrast-to-noise under sparse LAT data; increasing scan angle most effective for ghosting reduction; trade-off between algorithmic sophistication and angular coverage
comments: Comprehensive algorithmic review; the finding that increasing scan angle dominates over algorithmic choice underscores fundamental LAT limitations and provides practical guidance for industrial CT.

model_io.model: IR algorithms: SIRT, CGLS, ASD-POCS, ML-EM
inputs: limited-angle sinogram data (thin-slab phantoms: printed circuit boards, aluminum disc)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Iterative reconstruction algorithms outperform filtered backprojection (FBP) in contrast-to-noise under sparse angular coverage
hypotheses.result: IR algorithms improved performance; ML-EM and ASD-POCS reduced ghosting vs. FBP; increasing total scan angle was most effective mitigation

title: Predicting utilization of emergency contraceptives in ethiopia and identifying its predictors using machine learning
task: Predicting emergency contraception utilization in Ethiopia via machine learning and explainable AI
key_results: SMOTE + Logistic Regression best model (AUC-ROC 0.85, Recall 0.85, Precision 0.72) on 2,334 women (4.4% prevalence); emergency contraception awareness (heard_emergency) strongest predictor, followed by media exposure and health facility discussions; recent reproductive events linked to non-use
comments: Excellent application of SMOTE for class imbalance and SHAP for interpretability in reproductive health; finding that knowledge gaps dominate over socioeconomic factors has strong policy implications.

model_io.model: Eight ML algorithms (Logistic Regression, decision trees, ensemble methods, etc.) with SMOTE balancing
SHAP explainability

hypotheses.hypothesis: Knowledge (emergency contraception awareness) is a stronger predictor of use than socioeconomic or geographic factors; media exposure and quality health-system contact are key complementary drivers
hypotheses.result: AUC-ROC 0.85 (Recall 0.85, Precision 0.72); emergency contraception awareness ranked first; media/health facility contact crucial; static demographics poor predictors

title: Delving into carbon dioxide frosting temperature in natural gas mixtures using hyperparameter optimized gradient boosting decision trees
task: Prediction of CO₂ frosting temperature in natural gas mixtures
key_results: GBDT with Bayesian Probability Improvement (BPI) hyperparameter tuning: R² 0.9903, MSE 1.75%; SHAP confirmed thermodynamic consistency (increased CO₂/pressure raise frosting T; methane lowers it)
comments: Excellent integration of domain physics with ML interpretation; BPI's superiority over other hyperparameter methods is well-motivated for this narrowly-constrained regression task.

model_io.model: GBDT with Bayesian Probability Improvement (BPI) tuning
inputs: CO₂ concentration, system pressure, methane concentration, 430 experimental data points

model_io.model: SHAP explainability

hypotheses.hypothesis: BPI hyperparameter tuning outperforms alternatives by balancing exploration and exploitation, preventing overfitting in cryogenic phase transition prediction
hypotheses.result: GBDT-BPI achieved R² 0.9903 with thermodynamically-consistent SHAP attributions

title: Data-driven and experimental optimization of thermal performance in ZrO₂ Nanofluid oscillating heat pipes
task: Thermal performance optimization of ZrO₂-nanofluid oscillating heat pipes via RSM and machine learning
key_results: Response Surface Methodology + Box–Behnken design on thermal resistance (TR) and heat transfer coefficient (HTC); KNN, SVM, XGBoost models compared; optimal conditions: ~2 wt.% ZrO₂, 80% fill ratio, 35 W heat input → TR 1.03°C/W, HTC ~222 W/m²·°C; heat input and fill ratio dominant factors
comments: Well-structured experimental-ML pipeline; ANOVA identifies dominant factors, though the relatively weak effect of nanoparticle concentration (1–3 wt.%) may indicate limited scope of investigation.

model_io.model: Box–Behnken experimental design + RSM
ML models: KNN, SVM, XGBoost

hypotheses.hypothesis: Heat input and fill ratio are the dominant factors influencing OHP thermal performance; nanoparticle concentration has less significance
hypotheses.result: ANOVA and RSM confirmed dominance of heat input and fill ratio; XGBoost outperformed KNN and SVM; optimum at 2 wt.% ZrO₂, 80% fill, 35 W

title: Evidence-theoretic multi-sensor fusion with spatial semantic coupling for real-time hazard assessment in dynamic construction environments
task: Multi-sensor hazard assessment and risk quantification in dynamic construction environments
key_results: Credibility-weighted evidence fusion (Jousselme distance) achieves F1 0.862–0.842 vs. 0.743 (Dempster–Shafer); spatial-semantic 3D model with occlusion correction: grade-agreement 0.848 vs. 0.749; adaptive warning reduces miss rate 0.251→0.168; end-to-end latency ≤437 ms@500 nodes
comments: Comprehensive real-time framework addressing conflicting sensor inputs and spatial reasoning; validation on reproducible benchmarks and simulated scenarios strengthens claims, though field deployment metrics (false positive rate, user trust) remain unmeasured.

model_io.model: Credibility-weighted evidence fusion (Jousselme distance)
Spatial-semantic risk quantification with 3D building representation
Adaptive 4-level warning strategy (exponential moving average self-correction)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Jousselme distance-based fusion outperforms classical Dempster–Shafer under high-conflict sensor inputs
hypotheses.result: Fusion F1 0.862–0.842 vs. 0.743; spatial model with occlusion correction achieved grade-agreement 0.848 vs. 0.749

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adaptive warning thresholds reduce dynamic risk evolution miss rates compared to static thresholds
hypotheses.result: Adaptive strategy reduced miss rate from 0.251 to 0.168

title: Development of a mixture of experts with optimized EfficientNet features (MoEffNet)-powered automated identification system for images of agricultural equipment
task: Automated agricultural equipment identification from images
key_results: 98.72% Top-1 accuracy on 18,742-image dataset of 12 machinery types; outperforms EfficientNet-B4, Vision Transformers, and AMTNet
comments: The Mixture of Experts routing mechanism with Refined Addax metaheuristic optimization is well-motivated for agricultural imagery, though the 98.72% figure should be validated on held-out test sets separate from the public dataset partition.

Refined Addax Optimization Algorithm (RAOA)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dynamic routing via Mixture of Experts improves feature extraction for machinery subclasses under occlusion and environmental variability
hypotheses.result: MoEffNet achieved 98.72% accuracy and outperformed baselines; Grad-CAM showed focus on discriminative machinery parts

title: Research on assessment and adaptive correction technology of power system protection fixed value mismatch
task: Adaptive protection setting optimization in distribution networks with overlapping fast-tripping zones
key_results: Constrained multi-objective particle swarm optimization resolves protection mismatches; adaptive sectionalizing circuit-breaker placement addresses dead-zone problem via MATLAB validation
comments: The framework is solid for power systems but lacks public benchmark datasets and comparative validation against heuristic or industrial baselines.

model_io.model: Constrained multi-objective backbone PSO + K-means clustering

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multi-objective PSO with K-means clustering effectively resolves protection setting mismatches in overlapping fast-tripping zones

title: Multistage advanced persistent threat detection and malware attribution using Mamba state space models with Kolmogorov Arnold networks
task: Multi-stage advanced persistent threat detection and malware attribution via Mamba state-space and Kolmogorov-Arnold networks
key_results: MambaKAN-APT on DAPT 2020 network-flow benchmark (macro-F1 ~0.758 XGBoost vs. deep models competitive); CyberScienceLab malware attribution (balanced): MambaKAN macro-F1 ~0.959 vs. XGBoost n-gram ~0.954 (paired t p=0.59, statistically tied); SHAP identifies flow/opcode n-grams as discriminative
comments: Methodologically transparent: authors report competitive XGBoost baselines and statistical ties rather than over-claiming sequential advantage. Combining Mamba SSMs and KAN is novel; the honest reporting of results (especially macro-F1 parity on balanced task) builds credibility.

model_io.model: MambaKAN-APT (Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks + Mamba SSM)
inputs: DAPT 2020: network-flow 64 CICFlowMeter features across 5 attack phases
CyberScienceLab: disassembled opcode sequences from 5 threat-actor groups

model_io.model: SHAP explainability
Focal Loss for class imbalance (DAPT 2020: 73.5% normal traffic)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mamba SSM + KAN architecture with selective state-space recurrence and learnable B-spline activations models long-range temporal APT sequences with linear O(L) complexity
hypotheses.result: DAPT 2020 macro-F1 competitive with XGBoost (0.758); CyberScienceLab macro-F1 ~0.959, statistically tied with XGBoost (p=0.59); SHAP identified flow and opcode n-grams as influential

title: Validation design governs reliability claims in well-log lithology prediction
task: Well-log lithology classification under realistic deployment conditions
key_results: Row-level validation F1-macro 0.81–0.93 overstates unseen-well reliability (LOWOCV: 0.31–0.45); per-well mean 0.187–0.245 on 12-class taxonomy; metric choice and well-level evaluation critical
comments: This paper provides essential methodological guidance: the vast gap between row-level and well-level metrics exposes a common but problematic evaluation mismatch in deployed geoscience models.

model_io.model: Tree classifiers with context-aware and numeric features
inputs: well-log curves from 118 wells (Norwegian Continental Shelf)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Row-level validation substantially overestimates field deployment generalization to unseen wells
hypotheses.result: Leave-one-well-out F1-macro 0.31–0.45 vs. row-level 0.81–0.93; minority-class, mixed-lithology, and per-well failures persistent across configurations

title: Vibration serviceability assessment and vibration mitigation of through-truss footbridges in Iran under human-induced excitation
task: Vibration serviceability assessment and mitigation of through-truss steel footbridges under pedestrian excitation
key_results: Free-vibration calibration confirms numerical models; all vertical/longitudinal modes in critical range; under dense traffic, vertical acceleration >2.50 m/s² (unacceptable) in all bridges; TMD achieves 83% vertical acceleration reduction for critical traffic class; frequency-detuned TMD yields 61–86% reduction across traffic classes
comments: Rigorous experimental-numerical coupling with practical mitigation strategies; the frequency-detuned TMD design is a valuable engineering contribution for varying pedestrian masses.

model_io.model: Finite element model (FEM) with experimental calibration
inputs: measured natural frequencies from free-vibration tests

model_io.model: Tuned mass damper (TMD) and pier stiffness optimization

hypotheses.hypothesis: TMD tuned to critical traffic class reduces maximum vertical acceleration by >80%; frequency-detuned TMD maintains 61–86% reduction across varying pedestrian masses
hypotheses.result: Single-tuned TMD: 83% reduction for critical class; frequency-detuned TMD: 61–86% across all examined conditions

title: Heterogeneous performance of machine learning models in financial market forecasting

key_results: Ensemble methods (RF, GBM) capture nonlinear dynamics better; Ridge/Lasso excel on stable, high-correlation markets; no single algorithm dominates across VIX, S&P 500, gold, NG-F, Brent-F
comments: The finding of heterogeneous performance is sound but unsurprising; the paper would benefit from deeper analysis of which market properties (volatility clustering, regime switches) trigger method switching.

outputs: VIX, S&P 500, gold price, NG-F, Brent-F forecasts

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ensemble methods provide greater flexibility in nonlinear market interactions than linear regularized methods
hypotheses.result: RF and GBM outperformed Ridge and Lasso on markets with complex dynamics; Ridge/Lasso dominated stable markets with high predictor correlation
